statement: Ordinary BC_p acyclicity equals reversible BC_p asphericity on simply connected primary H-spaces; the A.4 equality is equivalent to ordinary acyclicity on a proper countable H-space domain
depends_on: A34.2; A4.2; Bousfield1996 Key Lemma1.6 and finite-product preservation; James1955 Theorem5.6
notes: Retains countability before nullification; Sigma BC_p is excluded from the H-space domain by its primitive cohomology classes. The equivalent nontrivial null-H-space formulation has no countability assertion for P H. Principal equality, third-element and full-fibre-size statuses remain open; no priority claim.

statement: Finite generation of mod-p cohomology as an unstable Steenrod algebra forces ordinary BC_p acyclicity for simply connected primary sphere-null H-spaces
depends_on: A4.5 preservation; published CCS Theorem7.2; UCT; injectivity of Prüfer group; Postnikov obstruction theory
notes: Applies at every prime; does not replace finite generation by degreewise finite type. The theorem eliminates this subfamily from the countable H-space gate, while the full equality and fibre-size questions remain open.

statement: Finite nonzero mod-p cohomology yields a finite primary aspherical complex; finite Steenrod-generation primary H-space additions to BC_p produce only the two endpoints
depends_on: Hatcher4C.1; rechecked REVLOC D3.3; AM1999 2.1/3.1/4.1; Bousfield2001 4.8; BHM2021 3.1; Levy3.2; CCS7.2
notes: Finite addition is rechecked supplied background. New extraction and endpoint dichotomy do not assert a uniform presentation of arbitrary localizers or settle the third-element/full-fibre-size questions.

statement: For each finite m and connected X finite iterated loop-suspension replacement preserves the least reversible class; primary classes admit simply connected double-loop presentations
depends_on: May1972 Proposition2.6 Corollary4.6 Theorem6.1; cofiber extension and pointed homotopy-colimit closure; adjunction retract
notes: Uses actual unstable equivariant filtration rather than only stable splitting. No finite Steenrod generation or uniform set-size bound; no infinite-m converse. Same-hour structural refinement.
